brief:
The stone-cutting workshops of the West Bank operate at a fraction of normal capacity as blockades disrupt markets, the Palestine News Network reported. Heavy industrial saws that once ran continuously now sit largely idle, leaving the sector crippled by restricted movement and trade.

Experts are turning attention to Gaza's rubble as a potential source of stone for reconstruction efforts, though the conflict has devastated both Palestinian economies dependent on the material trade.
dek: BETHLEHEM / West Bank In the stone-cutting workshops of the West Bank, heavy industrial saws that once hummed relentlessly now stand mostly silent, operating at barely a fraction of their capacity.
title: West Bank stone industry halts as blockades cut market access
